newsitem.title: GERMANY: PreussenElektra seeks Russian power - paper.
newsitem.headline: PreussenElektra seeks Russian power - paper.

text.p: German electricity supplier PreussenElektra, a unit of Veba AG, is seeking a contract to import electricity from Russia, German Sunday newspaper Welt am Sonntag reported on Saturday.
In an article released ahead of publication in this week's edition, the newspaper said that PreussenElektra was already negotiating with the Russian government.

The proposed power line would start east of the Urals and cross Poland into Germany, it added. Russia was seeking a price of three or four pfennigs per kilowatthour delivered, less than half of the production price per unit in Germany, it said.
The newspaper quoted PreussenElektra management board chairman Hans-Dieter Harig as saying that he did not anticipate any problems in running such a power line through Poland.
"Our contacts there are very good," the paper quoted him as saying.

The newspaper said that special Russian technology allowing transfer at high voltage meant that the power could be transferred at up to 1.5 million volts. This compared with German technology which allowed transfer at a voltage of no more than 400,000 volts, it said.
